condition: Acute hemolytic transfusion reaction complicated by disseminated intravascular coagulation
evaluationParameters: Hemodynamic status and progression of bleeding/coagulation abnormalities
missingInformation: Pretransfusion and postreaction clerical compatibility checks, direct antiglobulin test result, repeat blood typing/crossmatch, baseline vital signs and laboratory values, current urine output rate, and response to fluid resuscitation
priorityActions: Maintain IV access with new tubing and administer isotonic normal saline to support blood pressure and renal perfusion
Notify the provider and blood bank immediately and initiate the transfusion-reaction workup, including returning the blood bag and tubing and obtaining required blood and urine specimens
reasoning: The abrupt transfusion-associated systemic symptoms and intravascular hemolysis strongly indicate an acute hemolytic transfusion reaction; simultaneous bleeding, thrombocytopenia, hypofibrinogenemia, and prolonged coagulation times indicate secondary DIC.

stemEvidence.stemFact: Fever, rigors, bilateral flank pain, hypotension, hemoglobinuria, and a sense of impending doom within 12 minutes of starting a red blood cell transfusion, followed by port-wine urine, elevated LDH and bilirubin, and haptoglobin <10 mg/dL
Worsening hypotension and oliguria with port-wine urine after the transfusion was stopped
Symptoms began within 12 minutes of starting the red blood cell transfusion
Worsening hypotension, oozing from puncture sites, platelets 104 ×10³/µL, fibrinogen 140 mg/dL, INR 1.8, and aPTT 52 seconds
